The cloak consists of a ring with inner radius of 4.1 cm and outer radius of 10 cm, divided into 14 layers with varying thickness.
The cloak is made of aluminum and works by inducing artificial anisotropy in the effective medium parameters.
2D numerical simulations predict cloaking for microwaves between 2.6 and 7 GHz, and for sound waves between 3 and 8 kHz.
3D electromagnetic simulations show a slightly narrower cloaking band of 2.6 to 7.8 GHz, likely due to 3D effects and the presence of a ground plane.
Experiments demonstrate reduced scattering, preserved wavefronts, and 10-30 dB field attenuation inside the cloak's core at the cloaking frequencies for both microwaves and acoustic waves.
The cloak can provide protection for objects placed inside its core, with the field reduced by up to 30 dB at the lower end of the cloaking band.
Unlike previous cloaks relying on resonant elements, this cloak achieves broadband performance through its specific geometry and induced anisotropy.
The homogenization approach involves deriving effective tensors of density and permittivity/permeability using volume averaging over the cloak's periodic structure.
The cloak works equally well for transverse electric microwaves, pressure acoustic waves, and linear surface water waves due to the similar mathematical models governing their propagation.
The cloak's performance is better at the lower end of the cloaking band, with up to 30 dB field reduction at 2.6 GHz compared to 13 dB at 6 GHz for microwaves.
The cloak's height is not large compared to the wave wavelength, yet it still behaves as expected, demonstrating the robustness of the homogenization approach.
The cloak can be viewed as a multiphysics device, as it works for acoustic, electromagnetic, and water waves using the same underlying design principles.
The cloak's ability to control multiple wave types could have interesting applications in the emerging field of phoxonics.
The experimental results confirm the numerical predictions and validate the homogenization-based design approach for this broadband, multi-wave cloak.
The cloak's performance suggests it could be scaled up to provide protection against larger-scale waves, such as ocean waves.
